claims.text: The initial material is an equiatomic random solid solution of HfNbTaTiZr.
Random HfNbTaTiZr has significant local lattice distortion caused by atomic-size mismatch.
The random alloy strongly scatters phonons across the entire frequency spectrum.
Thermal annealing or Monte Carlo simulation can induce chemical short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr.
The induced SRO nucleates percolating B2-like HfTi and TiZr clusters.
Annealing between 0.5 and 0.8 Tm permits SRO formation without full phase separation.
Processing at 1 atm with suitable cooling rates can trap the percolative SRO state.
Atomic-radius matching in the HfTi and TiZr pairs allows B2-like clusters to relax local lattice strain.
The relaxed ordered clusters constitute low-distortion pathways for phonon transport.
Transition from the random state to B2-like order reduces the local variance in atomic-size mismatch.
Reduced local lattice distortion decreases the scattering cross-section for high-frequency phonons.
Percolation of low-distortion regions increases high-frequency phonon mean free paths enough to override scattering from the random matrix and cluster boundaries.
Percolating B2-like SRO produces a net increase in lattice thermal conductivity relative to the random HfNbTaTiZr alloy.
The conductivity increase is driven by enhanced group velocity and lifetime of phonons above 5 THz.
Low-frequency phonon scattering remains dominant but contributes less to total thermal resistance because of the enhanced high-frequency contribution.
Random HfNbTaTiZr exhibits minimal thermal conductivity because of severe phonon scattering from random atomic-size mismatch and lack of order.
The conductivity-increase regime occurs only after the ordered clusters exceed a percolation threshold.
Macroscopic phase separation or large coherent precipitates introduce sufficient interface scattering to restore a conductivity decrease.
Atoms inside the ordered clusters should have lower mean-square displacement than atoms in the random matrix.
Ordering should narrow rather than broaden high-frequency phonon DOS or spectral linewidth features.
